label: Lightfoot & Harmer · Greek
detail: The Apostolic Fathers (1891), Greek text, pp. 217–225

license.name: Public domain in the US, UK and EU

source.label: Internet Archive: Cornell University Library copy (1907 reprint)

italics: Lightfoot sets Scripture quotations in the Greek in uncial (capital-form) type; shown here in a distinct style.

preserves: printed wording, spelling, capitalization, punctuation and accentuation, as printed
page breaks of the printed edition
uncertain readings, marked ⟦?…⟧ and left unresolved
Lightfoot's chapter numerals and verse numbers exactly as printed (XVI has verses 1–7 only)
accents, breathings and iota subscripts as printed, including forms an editor would correct

normalizations.how: Victorian spacing before ; : ? ! removed. No other punctuation changed.
Print line breaks not kept; paragraphs kept. Line-end hyphenation joined; a word divided across a page break stays divided, with its printed hyphen.
A drop capital and the small capitals after it are written as ordinary capitals and not lowered.
Where the roman/italic status of adjoining punctuation cannot be seen at scan resolution, it goes inside the span if within the quotation, else outside (7 places, listed as open questions).
Text set in uncial type is transcribed in ordinary lowercase with σ/ς and the accents and breathings as printed.

edition.basis: Lightfoot & Harmer (1891). J. B. Lightfoot died 1889, J. R. Harmer died 1944. Assessed for the intended markets only (United States, United Kingdom, European Union); other countries not assessed.

digitization.basis: SCRIPTORIAS's own transcription from Internet Archive page images of two copies; no third-party transcription copied (Wikisource used for comparison only). No copyright is claimed in the historical text.

notices.publicDomain: **Public domain.** This is a transcription of J. B. Lightfoot and J. R. Harmer, *The Apostolic Fathers* (London: Macmillan, 1891), Greek text, pp. 217–225. It is in the public domain in the United States, where it was published in 1891, and in the United Kingdom and the European Union, where copyright ended 70 years after the death of its last author (J. B. Lightfoot died in 1889, J. R. Harmer in 1944). Its status in other countries has not been assessed. SCRIPTORIAS claims no copyright in this text.
notices.sources: Transcribed from page images of the Cornell University Library copy (a 1907 reprint of the second edition) and checked page by page against the University of Toronto copy (1891); no differences were found on these pages. Both copies were digitized by the Internet Archive: [Cornell copy](https://archive.org/details/cu31924024254744) · [Toronto copy](https://archive.org/details/apostolicfathers00lighuoft). Verified against the University of California copy (1898 printing) via HathiTrust: [HathiTrust copy](https://hdl.handle.net/2027/uc2.ark:/13960/t7zk5j13p). SCRIPTORIAS does not reproduce the page images. The transcription was prepared with AI assistance and internally checked against the page images. Page 235 was drafted from the Internet Archive's machine-read text and then corrected against both copies.

editorial.note: Internally checked transcription (docs/EDITORIAL.md §6), not independently verified. Open questions are shown with the text as provisional.

reviews.method: Internal check (docs/EDITORIAL.md §6), not an independent verification. Read from the page images of the Cornell copy (1907 reprint); every page compared word by word and mark by mark with the images and with the Toronto copy (1891 printing).

Internal check: edition, printing actually read (1907 reprint) and second copy (1891 printing), page and image indexes, and the size and SHA-256 of each transcription file recorded; sources linked externally, no page images hosted.
Internal check: all 16 chapters present, including the title and inscription; page joins continuous; nothing omitted.
Markup balanced; text.json rebuilds the transcription files byte for byte; refmap and alignment validate (npm run content:check, npm run test:content).
